summary: The study investigates the formation of high-k ZrO2 thin films on TiN substrates using atomic layer deposition (ALD) at 250°C. The films exhibit a high dielectric constant due to the formation of metastable tetragonal or cubic ZrO2 phases, which is attributed to growth-controlled selection rather than interfacial energy minimization. The crystalline structure of the films is influenced by the substrate's lattice mismatch and interfacial conditions.
evidence: ZrO2 thin films were grown by ALD using a traveling-wave-type reactor at a growth temperature of 250°C. Tetrakis(ethylmethylamido)zirconium (Zr(NEtMe)4) and O3 were used as the Zr and oxygen sources, respectively. The crystalline structure of the ZrO2 thin films was investigated by glancing angle incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD). The formation of the high-temperature phase of ZrO2 in ALD at such low temperatures is unclear, and the study aimed to investigate the possible reasons for the formation of the high-temperature form.
